proposedRoles.name: JM1 Marketing Function Runtime - Scoped
proposedRoles.rights: Exact operation union in functions[] only; enumerate Create/Read/Write/Append/AppendTo separately by table and operation. Do not grant Assign, Delete, Share, or Global on UserOwned tables unless a measured source path and an allowed/denied test requires it.
proposedRoles.orgOwnedTables: Entity metadata confirms jm1pub_titlemarketinghealths, jm1pub_productionassets, jm1pub_editorialapprovalgates, and jm1pub_editorialartifacts are OrganizationOwned. Grant Global only for the exact operation set required by each Function: title marketing health Read/Create/Write; production assets Read/Create/Write; editorial gates Read; editorial artifacts Read.
proposedRoles.executionlogs: Read/create privileges needed by publishingAssetEventOutboxTimer remain Local candidate: all 55,299 currently observed rows are HQ-owned. Prove page-boundary behavior on full dataset; do not use Global by default.

proposedRoles.name: JM1 One Intake Runtime - Scoped
proposedRoles.rights: Create/read/write only the intake receipt, contact, lead, and exact parent-contact/owner relationship operations listed in onePublicIntake. No Marketing Function, social publishing, catalog write, or administrative privileges.
proposedRoles.leadScope: Deep (Parent:Child Business Units) Read/Create/Write only for Lead is required to reconcile existing HQ and two JMF child-BU leads, unless owner-map/assignment design changes and live tests prove an equally complete narrower design. Assign and team Read/AppendTo require exact named owner-target checks; omit otherwise.
proposedRoles.contactScopeDecision: Live distribution is currently 5,799 HQ-owned contacts and none observed in child BU. Local Read is sufficient only if Dataverse duplicate detection/alternate-key or an enforced HQ ownership invariant closes cross-BU duplicate creation. Otherwise exact-email duplicate lookup requires Deep Read and exposes all Contact rows/columns allowed by Dataverse table privilege; field-level filtering in application code is not a security boundary. Do not adopt Contact Deep until Security explicitly accepts this residual access or approves a narrow server-side resolver/alternate-key design.

requiredPreCutoverProof: Create each MI application user separately; read back app ID/object ID, system user ID, business unit, enabled state, and exact role IDs.
For every operation/table/depth in approved matrices, run allowed read/create/update/relationship tests against synthetic rows; verify organization-owned tables separately.
Run denied tests for Contact outside approved scope, unrelated Leads, Delete/Assign/Share, Publishing title mutation, identity administration, and every table absent from the matrix.

Run actual Function timer and One intake canaries using each host MI; prove durable receipt, safe replay, social read/write where applicable, bounded failure state, and logs free of private inquiry content.

Compare RetrieveUserPrivileges and actual record operations; reconcile indirect team/security-role access and field security. Retain prior shared authority until both workloads pass, then remove only its exact overbroad role through an independently verified rollback-ready change.
explicitOpenDecisions: Dataverse Security/OPS owner must approve Contact cross-BU duplicate-resolution approach: narrow resolver/alternate key plus Local Contact scope, or accept Deep Contact Read on One intake identity.
Dataverse Security/OPS owner must approve the exact Global privilege set on all four OrganizationOwned tables, split by Function operation, and confirm Local closeout scan scope.

rules: Read and write only operations present in source paths.
Use Local for HQ-owned rows unless a demonstrated query or relationship needs broader reach.
Do not add Global merely because the existing shared application user has System Administrator.
No Custom API Execute is performed by the eight Functions or public intake route.
No Dataverse EntityDefinitions metadata read is required by entitySet() after this change.
Storage, Meta, LinkedIn, and ACS permissions are separate authorities and are not implied by this Dataverse matrix.
